title: How Long a Corporate Catering Service Agreement Has Run, and the Window Its Catering Spend Is Counted Over
content:
The counting window over which the catering spend invoiced on a Corporate Catering Service Agreement is measured turns on how long the agreement has been in force on the day the invoice is raised.

**Where the agreement has been in force for 24 months (two years) or more on that day**, the catering spend is counted over the 12 months ending on that day.

**Where the agreement has been in force for at least 12 months (a year) but fewer than 24 months on that day**, the catering spend is counted over the 6 months ending on that day.

**Otherwise**, the catering spend is counted over the 3 months ending on that day.

### Points of judgement

*From what is the age of the agreement taken?* From the day the agreement started, as the agreement record shows it, to the day the invoice is raised.

*An agreement that has run for exactly 24 months on the day the invoice is raised.* It has been in force for 24 months or more, so its catering spend is counted over the 12 months ending on that day.

*An agreement that has run 23 months.* It has not reached 24 months, but it has reached 12, so its catering spend is counted over the 6 months ending on that day.

*An agreement that has run for exactly 12 months.* It has reached 12 months and has not reached 24, so its catering spend is counted over the 6 months ending on that day.

*An agreement that has run 11 months.* It has not reached 12 months, so its catering spend is counted over the 3 months ending on that day.

| Months the agreement has been in force on the day the invoice is raised | Window the catering spend is counted over |
| --- | --- |
| 24 or more | 12 months ending on that day |
| At least 12 and fewer than 24 | 6 months ending on that day |
| Fewer than 12 | 3 months ending on that day |
